newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P 500 futures on GLOBEX down nearly 8 points.
newsitem.headline: S&P 500 futures on GLOBEX down nearly 8 points.

text.p: The key December Globex S&P 500 stock futures traded on GLOBEX were down nearly eight points in late Tokyo trading due to a U.S. newspaper report pointing to fears that the Japanese government and other governments may reduce their purchases of U.S. Treasuries.
At 0801 GMT, it was down 7.50 points at 740.50.
Earlier in the day, the index fell as low as 736.00, partly prompted by rumours that the Wall Street Journal was going to run a report which would be negative for U.S. markets.

The newspaper reported on Wednesday that some traders are saying there is cause to question whether Japanese institutions, known for buying U.S. Treasury debt securities over the past 18 months, will continue doing so.
Foreign governments, including Japan, have bought three-quarters or more of all new securities issued by the U.S. government over the past year, the story said.
The story quotes Goldman Sachs International vice-chairman Robert Hormats as saying Japanese institutions will likely slow their purchases, which could begin to push up interest rates.
"It could be the Achilles' heel of the bond and stock markets," Hormats told the newspaper.
